questions.q: A small particle moves to position <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> from its initial position <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mover><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> under the action of force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mover><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>. The value of work done will be ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Work done by a constant force is given by W=ForceF→·Displacementr→, where, r→=r→2-r→1

Given here, r1→=5i^-2j^+k^ and r→2=2i^+3j^-4k^

So, W=F→·r→2-r→1

=(5i^+2j^+7k^)·(5i^-2j^+k^)-(2i^+3j^-4k^)

⇒W=40 J

questions.q: Two particles having masses <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>16</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> respectively are moving with equal kinetic energies. The ratio of the magnitudes of their linear momentum is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>:</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> will be ___.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
p122×4=p222×16

p1p2=12

questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is initially at rest. It starts moving unidirectionally under the influence of a source of constant power <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math>. Its displacement in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msqrt><mi>P</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> will be ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy provided will be used to increase kinetic energy of the body. Therefore,

12mV2=Pt

V=2Ptm

⇒dxdt=2Ptm⇒∫0xdx=2Pm∫04t12dt

⇒x=2Pm23t3204

⇒x=16P3=13×16P

Hence, required value of α=4.

questions.q:
A rolling wheel of 12 kg is on an inclined plane at position P and connected to a mass of 3 kg through a string of fixed length and pulley as shown in figure.
Consider PR as friction free surface.
The velocity of centre of mass of the wheel when it reaches at the bottom Q of the inclined plane PQ will be 12xgh m s-1. The value of x (rounded off to the nearest integer) is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If we take the wheel as a ring then its moment of inertia will be, I=Mr2.

Using mechanical energy conservation,

Mgh-mgh=12mv2+12Mv2+12Iω2⇒12gh-3gh=123v2+1212v2+1212r2v2r2

⇒9gh=15v2+12v22

⇒v=23gh=1283gh

Therefore, x=83≃3

questions.q: A force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>)</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> acts on a particle. The work done by this force when the particle is moved from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is ________<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
F=(5y+20)j^

ω=∫Fdy=∫010(5y+20)dy

=5y22+20y010

=52×100+20×10

=250+200=450 J

questions.q: If the maximum load carried by an elevator is 1400 kg (600 kg-Passengers +800 kg-elevator) , which is moving up with a uniform speed of 3 m s-1 and the frictional force acting on it is 2000 N, then the maximum power used by the motor is _____________kW. g=10 m s-2
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The maximum force acting is, Fmax=14000+2000 N

= 16000 N

The formula for power is given by, P=Fmaxv.

It is given, v=3 m s-1.

⇒P = 16000 N × 3 m s-1 = 48000 W=48 kW

⇒W = 48 kW

questions.q: A solid circular disc of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> rolls along a horizontal floor so that its center of mass has a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The absolute value of work done on the disc to stop it is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using work-energy theorem, we get

W=∆KE

⇒W=0-12mv2+12Iω2

⇒W=0-12mv21+K2R2

=-12×50×0.421+12=-6 J

Absolute work =+6 J

Therefore, required value of W=6 J

questions.q: A force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo></math> acts on a particle in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math>-direction, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi></math> is newton and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> is in meter. The work done by the force during a displacement from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If an object is moved by certain distance by the application of an external force along the direction of the force, then the force is said to perform some work.

Given, the force exerted on the object is

F=5+3y2

The formula to calculate the work done W by the force in moving the object from a position y1 to another position y2 can be written as

W= ∫y1y2Fdy..........................(1)

Substitute the values into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required work done by the force.

W=∫255+3y2dy=5y+3y3325=132

questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> begins to move under the action of a time dependent force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>F</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mi>t</mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> are the unit vectors along <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> axis. The power developed by above force, at the time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>, will be _______<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, F→=ti^+3t2j^ N and m=1 kg

Now, we can write from Newton's second law, F→=ma→=mdv→dt

Then, dv→=ti^+3t2j^dt

Integrating the above, 

∫0vdv→=∫0tti^+3t2j^dt⇒v→=t22i^+t3j^

Now, power developed by the force is P=F→·v→=ti^+3t2j^·t22i^+t3j^

=t32+3t5

At t=2 s, power is P=232+325=4+3×32=100 W

questions.q: A particle m=1kg slides down a frictionless track AOC starting from rest at a point A (height 2m ). After reaching C, the particle continues to move freely in air as a projectile. When it reaching its highest point P (height 1m ), the kinetic energy of the particle (in J ) is: (Figure drawn is schematic and not to scale; take g=10ms-2 ) ______________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
KEP-KEA=PEP-PEA=mghP-mghA
=1×10×2-1×10×1=10J

questions.q: A block of mass 'm' (as shown in figure) moving with kinetic energy E compresses a spring through a distance 25 cm when, its speed is halved. The value of spring constant of used spring will be nE N m-1 for n=_____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using work - energy theorem

Wnet=∆KE

Wnet =Kf-Ki

⇒-12Kx2=12mv22-12mv2⇒-12Kx2=E4-E

⇒12Kx2=3E4⇒K=3E2x2

⇒K=3E2×142=24E N m-1

Thus, the value of n=24.

questions.q: A <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> mass takes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> to reach ground when dropped from a certain height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> above surface of earth. The loss of potential energy in the last second of fall is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. [Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Displacement in nth second is given by Sn=u+a22n-1

Here, displacement is 8th second is

S8=0+12×10×(2×8-1)

⇒S8=75 m

Loss of potential energy is 

ΔU=mgS8=0.4×10×75

⇒ΔU=300 J.

questions.q: A small block starts slipping down from a point B on an inclined plane AB, which is making an angle θ with the horizontal section BC is smooth and the remaining section CA is rough with a coefficient of friction μ. It is found that the block comes to rest as it reaches the bottom (point A) of the inclined plane. If BC=2AC, the coefficient of friction is given by μ=k tanθ. The value of k is .......
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let AC=ℓ  ∴  BC=2ℓ  ∴  AB=3ℓ

Apply work – Energy theorem

Wt+Wmg=ΔKE

mg(3ℓ)sinθ-μmgcosθ(ℓ)=0+0

μmgcosθℓ=3mg/sinθ

μ=3tanθ=ktanθ

k=3

questions.q: A ball of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>, moving with a velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, collides with a spring of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and force constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The length of the compressed spring is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo mathvariant="italic"> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>, to the nearest integer, is ___ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let's say the compression in the spring by:y. So, by work-energy theorem we have

⇒12mv2=12ky2⇒y=mk·v⇒y=4100×10⇒y=2 m

⇒ Final length of spring,=8-2=6 m.

questions.q: The potential energy <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>U</mi></mfenced></math> of a diatomic molecule is a function dependent on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> (interatomic distance) as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>U</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>α</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>10</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mi>β</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math> where, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>β</mi></math> are positive constants. The equilibrium distance between two atoms will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mfenced><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>α</mi></mrow><mi>β</mi></mfrac></mfenced><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mfrac></msup><mo>,</mo></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo></math>______ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For equilibrium

dUdr=0

-10αr11+5βr6=0

5βr6=10αr11

r5=2αβ

r5=2αβ

r=2αβ15a=1

questions.q: A car accelerates from rest of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The energy spent in this process is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. The energy required to accelerate the car from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>u</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mi>E</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy of a moving particle is given by

E=12mu2   ...(1)

When the final velocity of the particle becomes twice the initial velocity, the kinetic energy of the particle can be written as

nE=12m(2u)2-u2= 12m3u2   ...2

Divide equation (2) by equation (1) and solve to calculate the value of n.

nEE=12m3u212mu2⇒n=3

questions.q: A block is fastened to a horizontal spring. The block is pulled to a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from its equilibrium position (at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>) on a frictionless surface from rest. The energy of the block at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. The spring constant of the spring is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At first the block is pulled to a distance x0=10 cm(extreme position).

Potential energy of block is Ui=12kx02 and kinetic energy os block, Ki=0.

Now, when the block is at distance 5 cm.

Potential energy is Uf=12kx022 and kinetic energy is Kf=0.25 J

Total energy of block will be conserved, so 

12kx02+0=12kx024+0.25

⇒12kx0234=14

⇒12k3100=1⇒k=2003 N m-1

=67 N m-1

questions.q:
A ball of mass 100 g is dropped from a height h=10 cm on a platform fixed at the top of a vertical spring (as shown in figure). The ball stays on the platform and the platform is depressed by a distance h2. The spring constant is _____ N m-1
(Use g=10 m s-2)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Loss in the gravitational potential energy of the ball= gain in the potential energy by the spring

-∆PEgravitational=∆PEspring

mgh+h2=12kh22⇒mg3h2=kh28

⇒k=12mgh=12×0.1×100.1=120 N m-1

questions.q: A cricket ball of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is thrown vertically up by a bowling machine so that it rises to a maximum height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> after leaving the machine. If the part pushing the ball applies a constant force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> on the ball applies a constant force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi></math> on the ball and moves horizontally a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> while launching the ball, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>in</mi><mo> </mo><mi>N</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From work energy theorem F0.2-mg20=0

F=mg200.2

=mg2002

=0.15×10×2002

=150.00 N

questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is moving with a momentum of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Now a force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> acts on the body in the direction of its motion for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The increase in the Kinetic energy of the body is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the change on momentum of the object is given by

pf-pi=∫Fdt   ...1

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the final momentum of the object.

pf-10 kg m s-1=2 N×5 s⇒pf=10+10 kg m s-1= 20 kg m s-1

The formula to calculate increase in kinetic energy ∆K of the particle is given by

∆K=12mpf2-pi2   ...2

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (2) to calculate the required increase in kinetic energy.

∆K=12×5 kg×202-102 kg2 m2 s-2= 30 J
